title: T8 - Calibration
jupyter: python3
---


This tutorial drafts how we would set up a simple calibration workflow:

- define which data we want to fit the model to 
- set up a simulation object
- define which parameters and which parameter ranges we want to test
- run the calibration


```{python}
import starsim as ss
import typhoidsim as ty
```

We first make a function that will create a Sim object with the ingredients we believe explain our data, and over a span of time that matches that of our data. Inside this function you will see that we have wrapped the basic setup seen in many of the other tutorials. To keep this example simple and quick, there is no transmission (`exposure2contact_rate=0, teer=0`): the number infected is those infected at the start, until they recover, plus the chronic carriers, who stay infected.

The parameters to calibrate are given as `ss.par()` with the range to explore (`bounds`), and the value to start from. Here, the initial prevalence `init_prev` and the probability of becoming a chronic carrier given gallstones, `p_cpg`.

```{python}
def make_sim(init_prev=ss.par(0.05, bounds=[0.001, 0.1]), p_cpg=ss.par(0.05, bounds=[0.05, 0.4]), data=None, rand_seed=1):
    pars = dict(
        start    = 1982,          # Starting year
        dur      = ss.years(9),   # Duration of the simulation
        dt       = ss.weeks(1),   # Timestep of 1 week
        verbose  = 0,             # Do not print details of the run
        rand_seed = rand_seed,
    )
    typhoid = ty.Typhoid(init_prev=init_prev, p_cpg=p_cpg, exposure2contact_rate=0, teer=0)
    ppl = ss.People(10_000)

    sim = ss.Sim(
        pars=pars,
        people=ppl,
        diseases=typhoid,
        data=data, # The data to fit to
    )

    return sim
```

We usually have some data we'd like to fit the model to. The data below is simulated data using specific values for `init_prev` (0.01) and `p_cpg` (0.35). The simplest way to pass data for a calibration is in the form of a dataframe with a `date` column and columns named like the results of the `Sim`, for instance `typhoid.infected`, the number infected. `sim.to_data()` makes such a dataframe from a sim.

```{python}
truth = make_sim(init_prev=0.01, p_cpg=0.35, rand_seed=2).run()
data = truth.to_data('typhoid.infected')
data.head()
```

Now we put all the elements together: the sim with the data, calibrated with `sim.fit()`, which uses [Optuna](https://optuna.org/) to search the parameter ranges for the values whose results best match the data.

```{python}
sim = make_sim(data=data)
fit = sim.fit(method='optuna', n_trials=60, n_workers=4, verbose=0) # The trials run in parallel
fit.summarize()
```

```{python}
fit.plot();
```

The calibrated parameters are in `fit.pars`:

```{python}
fit.pars
```
